# voice


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

This module turns a spoken answer into text. With the local engines, the
audio does not go off the machine. The web app records while you talk.
It cuts the audio into segments at your pauses and sends each segment
here. This module transcribes the segments one at a time, in order. The
text goes into the think-aloud box while you continue to talk.

The module also speaks.
[`speak`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#speak) turns
one line of the screen guide into WAV audio, with the start time of each
word, so the board can light each word as it is said.

These are the imports of the module.

## Engines

There are two engines. `mlx` runs on this machine. `openai` sends the
audio to OpenAI.

- `mlx` runs any speech to text model that mlx-audio can load. The
  default is Qwen3-ASR 0.6B (8 bit, 1.0 GB). Whisper large-v3-turbo is
  the second model on the Settings page, and the search finds the
  others. Install mlx-audio with `pip install abhyasa[whisper]`.
- `openai` uses the OpenAI transcription API. It is off until you set a
  key. It sends the audio off the machine.

Each engine gets a hint: the name of the concept and its terms.
Qwen3-ASR reads it as hot words, Whisper as its initial prompt, and
OpenAI as its prompt.

The table gives the numbers on this machine (an M-series Mac), with each
model warm. “Clip A” is the English test clip of the model layer
(`rishi/nbs/speech.wav`). “Clip B” is a clip in a cloned voice with
Nyāya terms in IAST and technical terms. “Terms” is the fraction of the
9 key terms in clip B that the engine wrote correctly. “5 s” is the time
for one 5-second segment.

- “load” is a cold start of a cached model in a new process, with the
  Python imports. The first download takes longer.
- “memory” is the MLX peak.
- “Sanskrit CER” is the character error rate on a 9-second Nyāya sūtra
  (from vachaka), after the vachaka normalization.
- Moonshine gave no text for the 24-second clip A. It is good only for
  short segments.
- For Sanskrit speech, use Qwen3-ASR or Whisper with the hint, or
  vachaka.

Qwen3-ASR 0.6B is the default. With the hint, it has no errors on clip B
and it writes all 9 terms. One 5-second segment takes 0.14 s. Before
0.0.16, the default was Gemma 4 E4B on LiteRT. It had the same score,
but it was 5 times slower, and its model was 3.7 GB.

`DFLT_STT` is the default model of the `mlx` engine. The other constants
are the named models. `ALIASES` keeps the old engine names: `whisper`
and `parakeet` are the `mlx` engine with a fixed model. `gemma` was the
default engine before 0.0.16, so it becomes the `mlx` engine with the
default model. `POCKET` is the Hugging Face repo of the local voice (see
“A natural voice” below), and `POCKET_FILES` are the files of its
English model and of its default voice. The repo has many languages, so
abhyasa gets only these files.

## Settings

The settings are in `settings.json` in
[`cfg_dir()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/settings.html#cfg_dir).
The
[`settings`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/settings.html#settings)
module keeps the table of values and the file; this module uses its
`stt` section. The web app changes the settings, and the next segment
uses the change. You do not have to restart.

Without a file, you get the defaults. A change to one key keeps the
other keys.

``` python
test_eq({k: settings()['stt'][k] for k in ('engine', 'model', 'segment')}, dict(engine='mlx', model='', segment=True))
update_settings('stt', segment=False)
test_eq(val('stt.segment'), False)
update_settings('stt', segment=True)
```

[`current`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#current)
gives the engine and model in use. `$ABHYASA_STT` has priority over the
settings. It can be an engine (`mlx`), an old name (`whisper`, `gemma`),
or an engine and a model
(`mlx:mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo-asr-fp16`). An old settings
file with `gemma` and a LiteRT model gets the default model. Nothing
writes the file again.

### resolve

``` python
def resolve(
    engine:str, model:str=''
)->tuple:
```

*The engine and model for a name: aliases become `mlx`, `engine:model`
splits, an empty model gets the default.*

The settings give Qwen3-ASR by default. An old `gemma` setting gives the
same, also with its old model. The environment variable has priority.

``` python
test_eq(current(), ('mlx', DFLT_STT))
test_eq(resolve('gemma', 'litert-community/gemma-4-E4B-it-litert-lm'), ('mlx', DFLT_STT))
test_eq(resolve('parakeet'), ('mlx', DFLT_PARAKEET))
test_eq(resolve('mlx:mlx-community/whisper-tiny-asr-fp16'), ('mlx', 'mlx-community/whisper-tiny-asr-fp16'))
test_fail(lambda: resolve('kokoro'), contains='unknown')
os.environ['ABHYASA_STT'] = 'whisper'
test_eq(current(), ('mlx', DFLT_WHISPER))
os.environ['ABHYASA_STT'] = 'gemma'
test_eq(current(), ('mlx', DFLT_STT))
del os.environ['ABHYASA_STT']
```

## One model in memory

[`resident`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#resident)
keeps one model loaded in each slot: `stt` for speech to text, `tts` for
the speaking voice. When the app asks for a different model in a slot,
it frees the old model of that slot first. Two large models for the same
job in memory at the same time can make the Mac slow.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/voice.py#L65"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### resident

``` python
def resident(
    key, load, close:NoneType=None, slot:str='stt'
):
```

*The loaded model of `slot` for `key`: when `key` is new, free the old
model of the slot, then `load()` the new one.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/voice.py#L54"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### unload

``` python
def unload(
    slot:str='stt'
):
```

*Free the loaded model of `slot`: `stt` (speech to text) or `tts` (the
speaking voice).*

A new key frees the old model. The same key does not load again. A model
in the `tts` slot does not free the model in the `stt` slot.

``` python
freed = []
resident('a', lambda: 'A', freed.append)
test_eq(resident('a', lambda: 'other'), 'A')
test_eq(resident('b', lambda: 'B'), 'B')
test_eq(freed, ['A'])
test_eq(resident('k', lambda: 'K', slot='tts'), 'K')
test_eq((resident('b', lambda: 'other'), freed), ('B', ['A']))
unload(); unload('tts')
```

Each engine is a function that takes a WAV path, a hint and a model, and
returns text.

The `mlx` engine gives the hint to a model that accepts one: Whisper as
`initial_prompt`, Qwen3-ASR as `hotwords`.

A Whisper-like model gets `initial_prompt`. A Qwen3-like model gets a
list of hot words. A model without either gets nothing.

``` python
class _W:
    def generate(self, audio, initial_prompt=None): pass
class _Q:
    def generate(self, audio, hotwords=None): pass
test_eq(_hint_kw(_W(), 'Nyāya, hetu'), dict(initial_prompt='Nyāya, hetu'))
test_eq(_hint_kw(_Q(), 'Nyāya, hetu'), dict(hotwords=['Nyāya', 'hetu']))
test_eq(_hint_kw(_W(), ''), {})
```

## OpenAI

The `openai` engine posts the WAV to the OpenAI transcription API, with
the hint as its
[`prompt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/prompts.html#prompt).
`http_post` is `httpx.post` unless a test puts a fake in its place.

The key comes from the first of these places that has `OPENAI_API_KEY`:
the environment, the abhyasa `keys.env`, then the ramabana `keys.env`.
ramabana says where its file is (`$RAMABANA_CONFIG`, else
`~/.config/ramabana/keys.env`). abhyasa reads both files with ramabana’s
`load_keys`. It refuses a file that other users can read, and it runs
`!command` values. abhyasa only reads the ramabana file.
[`set_openai_key`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#set_openai_key)
writes the abhyasa file with `save_key` (atomic, mode 0600). ramabana is
an optional extra. Without it, abhyasa reads and writes plain
`NAME=value` lines.
[`masked`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#masked)
shows only the last 4 characters.

### openai_key

``` python
def openai_key()->tuple:
```

*The OpenAI key and where it is from; `('', '')` when there is none.*

A key in the abhyasa file comes back with its source, and the file has
mode 0600. When the abhyasa file has no key, abhyasa reads the ramabana
file. This test points ramabana to a temp folder.

``` python
os.environ['RAMABANA_CONFIG'] = str(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'config.toml')
test_eq(openai_key(), ('', ''))
keys_path().write_text('export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-ramabana-0000"\n'); keys_path().chmod(0o600)
test_eq(openai_key(), ('sk-ramabana-0000', str(keys_path())))
test_eq(os.getenv('OPENAI_API_KEY'), None)
set_openai_key('sk-test-1234')
test_eq(openai_key(), ('sk-test-1234', str(cfg_dir()/'keys.env')))
test_eq(oct((cfg_dir()/'keys.env').stat().st_mode & 0o777), '0o600')
test_eq(masked('sk-test-1234'), '…1234')
```

The engine sends the model, the hint and the WAV, with the key in the
header. This test uses a fake HTTP client.

``` python
class _R:
    def raise_for_status(self): pass
    def json(self): return dict(text='hetu and sādhya')
sent = {}
def fake_post(url, **kw): sent.update(url=url, **kw); return _R()
http_post = fake_post
p = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'a.wav'; p.write_bytes(b'RIFF')
test_eq(_openai(p, 'hetu'), 'hetu and sādhya')
test_eq(sent['data'], dict(model=DFLT_OPENAI, response_format='json', prompt='hetu'))
test_eq(sent['headers']['Authorization'], 'Bearer sk-test-1234')
set_openai_key('')
keys_path().unlink()
test_fail(lambda: _openai(p), contains='no OpenAI key')
http_post = None
```

A key with a newline or a space can add a second line to the file. Thus
[`set_openai_key`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#set_openai_key)
refuses it.

``` python
test_fail(lambda: set_openai_key('sk-a\nOTHER=1'), contains='only letters')
test_fail(lambda: set_openai_key('sk a b c d e'), contains='only letters')
```

## Transcribe

[`transcribe`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#transcribe)
accepts a path or bytes. It writes bytes to a temporary file and removes
the file after use. Without an engine, it uses
[`current()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#current),
so a change on the Settings page applies to the next segment.

## Models

`KNOWN` lists the models that the Settings page shows first: the two
local models that we measured (see the table above), and two OpenAI
models.
[`cached`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#cached)

looks for its English model only.

[`model_size`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#model_size)
counts only the English files of the local voice. This test uses a fake
Hugging Face API, so it does not use the network.

``` python
class _Api:
    def list_models(self, **kw): return [AttrDict(id=i, downloads=n) for i, n in (('mlx-community/Kokoro-82M-bf16', 9), ('mlx-community/whisper-tiny-asr-fp16', 8))]
    def model_info(self, m, files_metadata=True): return AttrDict(siblings=[AttrDict(rfilename=f, size=10) for f in (*POCKET_FILES, 'languages/french/model.safetensors')])
test_eq(search_models('', api=_Api()), [dict(model='mlx-community/whisper-tiny-asr-fp16', downloads=8, size=40)])
test_eq(model_size(POCKET, _Api()), 30)
```

[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#fetch)
downloads a model and notes it in the settings. The local voice gets
only its English model and its default voice: it loads them, so they are
in memory for the first line.
[`remove`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#remove)
deletes a model from the cache, but only a model that
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#fetch)
downloaded. Other entries in the cache belong to other programs.

## A natural voice

The board of the screen guide says one line for each step. The browser
can say it with its own voice (`speechSynthesis`), but that voice sounds
like a machine.
[`speak`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#speak) gives
a natural voice. There are two engines:

- `pocket` runs Kyutai’s Pocket TTS on this Mac, with the pocket-tts-mlx
  package. The download is 225 MB. It has 21 English voices, and it
  makes a line of 4 seconds in less than 1 second. Install it with
  `pip install abhyasa[voice]`.
- `openai` sends the line to the OpenAI speech API. It is off until you
  set a key. Each line passes ramabana’s guard first.

`browser` is the third choice of the setting `voice.out`. Then the page
speaks, and this module makes no audio. The default is `pocket`. Until
its model is on this Mac, the browser speaks:
[`Speaker`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#speaker)
refuses the line with the word “browser”, and the page uses its own
voice.

Licences: the pocket-tts-mlx code is MIT. The Pocket TTS weights
(`kyutai/pocket-tts-without-voice-cloning`, by Kyutai) are CC-BY-4.0.

These are the defaults. `POCKET_VOICES` are the 21 English voices of
Pocket TTS. `caro_davy` is first: the owner chose it by ear. The OpenAI
voices are the voices of its speech API.

[`out_resolve`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#out_resolve)
fills in the default model and voice of an engine. Before 0.0.16 the
local voices were `kokoro` and `hf`: they become `pocket`, and a voice
that Pocket does not have becomes `caro_davy`. Thus an old settings file
works, and nothing writes it again.
[`out_current`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#out_current)
gives the voice of the settings, with its speed.
[`out_where`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#out_where)

test_eq(out_current(), ('pocket', POCKET, 'caro_davy', 1.))

test_fail(lambda: out_resolve('espeak'), contains='unknown')

### The time of each word

The board lights each word when the voice says it. Pocket TTS and OpenAI
give no word times. Thus
[`by_letters`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#by_letters)
shares the length of the audio among the words by their letters.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/voice.py#L264"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### by_letters

``` python
def by_letters(
    text:str, secs:float
)->list:
```

*A start time in seconds for each word of `text` in audio of `secs`
seconds: each word takes a share by its letters.*

Two words of 2 and 6 letters in 1 second: the first word starts at 0,
the second after 3/10 of the second.

``` python
test_eq(by_letters('is hidden', 1.), [0., .3])
test_eq(by_letters('', 1.), [])
```

### WAV

[`to_wav`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#to_wav)
makes WAV bytes (mono, 16 bit) from the float samples of a model.
[`clean_wav`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#clean_wav)
writes the header of a WAV again with its true length. OpenAI streams
its WAV, so its header can give a wrong length.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/voice.py#L280"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### clean_wav

``` python
def clean_wav(
    audio:bytes
)->bytes:
```

*`audio` with a header that gives the true length of its samples.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/voice.py#L272"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### to_wav

``` python
def to_wav(
    samples, rate:int
)->bytes:
```

*WAV bytes (mono, 16 bit) for float samples from -1 to 1.*

One second of samples at 24 kHz is one second of WAV. A header that says
the data is very long becomes a header with the true length.

``` python
test_eq(wav_seconds(to_wav([0.] * 24000, 24000)), 1.)
import struct
w = to_wav([0.] * 2400, 24000)
bad = w[:4] + struct.pack('<I', 0xFFFFFFFF) + w[8:40] + struct.pack('<I', 0xFFFFFFFF) + w[44:]   # as a stream: the RIFF and data sizes are unknown
test_eq(wav_seconds(clean_wav(bad)), .1)
```

### Pocket TTS

[`_pocket`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#_pocket)
loads the model one time into the `tts` slot of
[`resident`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#resident),
and keeps the state of each voice that it used.
[`_pocket_say`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#_pocket_say)
makes the audio of one line. `normalize=True` makes the voices equally
loud: some, such as `stuart_bell` and `peter_yearsley`, are quiet.
Pocket TTS has no speed, so the speed setting is only for OpenAI. When
pocket-tts-mlx is not installed, the error says how to install it.

### OpenAI

The `openai` engine posts the line to the OpenAI speech API and asks for
WAV. `instructions` can set the tone (“calm, like a teacher”); only the
`gpt-4o` models read it. The owner’s rule is that each text that goes to
a hosted model passes ramabana’s guard
([`abhyasa.guide.guard`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#guard),
with
[`ramabana.guard.outgoing`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/guard.html#outgoing)).
It masks a secret and refuses personal data when the privacy setting
says so.

### speak

[`speak`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#speak) gives
the WAV bytes of one line and the start time of each of its words.
Without an engine, it uses the voice of the settings. For the browser
voice, it refuses: the page speaks then.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/voice.py#L322"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### speak

``` python
def speak(
    text:str, engine:str=None, model:str=None, voice:str=None, speed:float=None, instructions:str=''
)->tuple:
```

*WAV bytes for `text`, and the start time in seconds of each of its
words (split on white space).*

### Tests with a fake model

A fake Pocket TTS: it gives 0.25 s of silence for each word, and it
notes each voice state that it makes. The loader is a fake too, so the
test downloads nothing.

``` python
import numpy as np
```

``` python
class _Pocket:
    sample_rate = 24000
    def __init__(self): self.said, self.voices = [], []
    def get_state_for_audio_prompt(self, v): self.voices.append(v); return dict(voice=v)
    def generate_audio(self, st, text, normalize=False):
        self.said.append((st['voice'], text, normalize))
        return np.zeros(6000 * len(text.split()), np.float32)
loads = []
_real_load, _pocket_load = _pocket_load, (lambda: loads.append(1) or (_Pocket(), {}))
```

[`speak`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#speak) gives
one second of WAV for four words, and a time for each word that goes up.
The second line does not load the model again, and a voice state loads
one time.

``` python
wav, words = speak('Noise goes in, slowly.', 'pocket')
test_eq(wav_seconds(wav), 1.)
test_eq(words, by_letters('Noise goes in, slowly.', 1.))
test_eq(words, sorted(words))
speak('Again.', 'pocket', voice='mary'); speak('Once more.', 'pocket', voice='mary')
pk = _slots['tts'][0].obj[0]
test_eq((loads, pk.voices, pk.said[-1]), ([1], ['caro_davy', 'mary'], ('mary', 'Once more.', True)))
```

The settings choose the voice when
[`speak`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#speak) has no
engine. The browser voice makes no audio here.

``` python
update_settings('voice', out='pocket', out_voice='paul')
speak('hello')
test_eq(pk.said[-1][0], 'paul')
update_settings('voice', out='browser', out_voice='')
test_fail(lambda: speak('hello'), contains='browser')
```

The OpenAI engine refuses with no key. With a key, it sends the text
after the guard, with the model, the voice and the tone. Here a fake
guard puts a mark on each text, so the test sees that each text passed
it.

``` python
import abhyasa.guide
```

``` python
real_guard, abhyasa.guide.guard = abhyasa.guide.guard, lambda s, model=None, mode=None: f'[{model.name}] {s}'
test_fail(lambda: speak('hello', 'openai'), contains='no OpenAI key')
set_openai_key('sk-test-1234')
class _W:
    content = to_wav([0.] * 12000, 24000)
    def raise_for_status(self): pass
sent = {}
http_post = lambda url, **kw: sent.update(url=url, **kw) or _W()
wav, words = speak('Look at the noise.', 'openai', instructions='calm, like a teacher')
test_eq(sent['url'], OPENAI_SPEECH_URL)
test_eq(sent['json'], dict(model=DFLT_SPEECH, voice='marin', input='[openai] Look at the noise.', response_format='wav', speed=1., instructions='[openai] calm, like a teacher'))
test_eq((wav_seconds(wav), len(words)), (.5, 4))
```

`tts-1` does not read `instructions`, so the engine does not send them.
Then the test puts back the real guard, the real HTTP client and the
real loader.

``` python
speak('Hi.', 'openai', 'tts-1', instructions='calm')
assert 'instructions' not in sent['json']
abhyasa.guide.guard, http_post = real_guard, None
set_openai_key('')
_pocket_load = _real_load
unload('tts')
```

### One worker for the voice

[`Speaker`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#speaker)
has one worker thread for all the calls of the speaking voice, separate
from the speech to text worker. Thus a line of the board does not wait
for a segment of dictation. It keeps the lines that it said in this run
(at most `most`), by engine, model, voice, speed and text. The board
asks for the same line again when the learner goes back a step, and that
line then comes at once. Two requests for the same line share one call.
`warm` loads the model in use with one short line, so the first line of
a board does not wait for the load. The browser voice and OpenAI have
nothing to load.

A model that is not on this Mac yet is not downloaded for a line: the
Settings page shows its download. Until then, `say` refuses the line
with the word “browser”, as for the browser voice, so the page and the
Mac app speak with their own voice.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/voice.py#L331"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Speaker

``` python
def Speaker(
    fn:NoneType=None, most:int=64, here:NoneType=None
):
```

*One worker thread for the speaking voice, and the lines that it said in
this run.*

A fake voice counts its calls. The same line comes from the cache, and a
new speed is a new line.

``` python
calls = []
def fake_speak(text, engine, model, voice, speed):
    calls.append((text, engine, voice, speed)); time.sleep(.02)
    return to_wav([0.] * 2400, 24000), by_letters(text, .1)
sk = Speaker(fake_speak, most=2, here=lambda m: True)
test_fail(lambda: sk.say('hi', engine='browser'), contains='browser')
r = sk.say('Look  here.', engine='pocket')
test_eq((r['cached'], r['where'], r['voice'], r['words']), (False, 'on this Mac', 'caro_davy', by_letters('Look here.', .1)))
test_eq(sk.say('Look here.', engine='pocket')['cached'], True)
sk.say('Look here.', engine='pocket', speed=1.5)
test_eq(len(calls), 2)
```

Two requests at the same time for a new line make one call. The cache
keeps at most `most` lines: the oldest goes first.

``` python
with ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as ex: list(ex.map(lambda _: sk.say('Both at once.', engine='pocket'), range(2)))
test_eq(len(calls), 3)
test_eq(len(sk.lines), 2)
test_eq(sk.say('Look here.', engine='pocket')['cached'], False)
```

A failed line is not kept. `warm` loads the voice of the settings one
time, and does nothing for the browser voice. A model that is not here
is not warmed, and a line for it says that the browser speaks.

``` python
sk = Speaker(lambda *a: 1 / 0, here=lambda m: True)
test_fail(lambda: sk.say('x', engine='pocket'))
test_eq(sk.lines, {})
update_settings('voice', out='browser')
test_is(Speaker(fake_speak).warm(), None)
update_settings('voice', out='pocket')
sk = Speaker(fake_speak, here=lambda m: True); calls.clear()
sk.warm().result(); test_is(sk.warm(), None)
test_eq((sk.status, calls), ('ready', [('Ready.', 'pocket', 'caro_davy', 1.)]))
sk = Speaker(fake_speak, here=lambda m: False)
test_is(sk.warm(), None)
test_fail(lambda: sk.say('x'), contains='browser')
```

## Segments in order

The browser sends one segment each time you stop to think.
[`Speech`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#speech) has
one worker thread for all the model calls. Thus only one model is in
memory, and the segments run one at a time, in the order they came. A
[`Dictation`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#dictation)
collects the segments of one answer. `next` gives the text in the order
of the segment numbers, also when a slow request arrives late. When the
browser sends a segment again (after an error), the code does not use it
two times.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/voice.py#L377"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Dictation

``` python
def Dictation(
    speech, hint:str=''
):
```

*The segments of one spoken answer: each is transcribed on the speech
worker, and the text comes out in order.*

[`Speech`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/voice.html#speech) owns
the worker. `warm` loads the model in use with half a second of silence,
so the first segment does not wait for it. `use` changes the engine and
model, saves the change, and warms the new model.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/voice.py#L413"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Speech

``` python
def Speech(
    fn:NoneType=None
):
```

*One worker thread for every speech model call, and the open
dictations.*

### Tests with a fake engine

This fake engine is slow on even segments, so the requests finish out of
order. The text must still come out in order.

``` python
calls = []
def slow_fake(audio, hint=''):
    n = int(audio.decode())
    calls.append(n)
    time.sleep(.05 if n % 2 == 0 else 0)
    return f'segment {n} ({hint})'
sp = Speech(slow_fake)
d = sp.runs[sp.start('hetu')]
```

Segments 0 to 5 arrive out of order, from several threads. Segment 3
comes two times.

``` python
order = [2, 0, 1, 3, 3, 5, 4]
with ThreadPoolExecutor(4) as ex: added = list(ex.map(lambda n: d.add(n, str(n).encode()), order))
test_eq(sum(added), 6)
d.stop(6)
out = []
while not (r := d.next(5)).get('done'): out.append(r)
test_eq([r['seq'] for r in out], list(range(6)))
test_eq(out[0]['text'], 'segment 0 (hetu)')
test_eq(sorted(calls), list(range(6)))
```

All the model calls ran on the one worker thread, one at a time.

``` python
seen = set()
sp.submit(lambda: seen.add(threading.current_thread().name)).result()
test_eq(len(seen), 1)
test_eq(d.pending, 0)
```

An engine error gives an empty text with the error. It does not stop the
segments after it.

``` python
def flaky(audio, hint=''):
    if audio == b'bad': raise RuntimeError('no model')
    return 'ok'
sp = Speech(flaky)
d = sp.runs[sp.start()]
d.add(0, b'bad'); d.add(1, b'good'); d.stop(2)
test_eq(d.next(5), dict(seq=0, text='', error='no model'))
test_eq(d.next(5), dict(seq=1, text='ok'))
test_eq(d.next(5), dict(done=True))
```

Without `stop`, `next` waits and then gives None. `use` saves the choice
and warms the new model with silence.

``` python
d = sp.runs[sp.start()]
test_is(d.next(.05), None)
heard = []
sp = Speech(lambda a, hint='': heard.append(wav_seconds(a)) or '')
sp.use('parakeet').result()
test_eq(current(), ('mlx', DFLT_PARAKEET))
test_eq(heard, [.5])
assert sp.status.startswith('ready'), sp.status
update_settings('stt', engine='mlx', model='')
```

## Real models

These tests use a real clip and real models. They are slow. Run them
with `nbdev-test --flags slow`.

``` python
clip = first(p for p in (Path('../../rishi/nbs/speech.wav'), Path('../../../rishi/nbs/speech.wav')) if p.exists())   # from the repo or a worktree
if clip:
    for e in ('mlx', 'whisper'): assert transcribe(clip, e, hint='Tennyson').strip(), e
    unload()
```

``` python
wav, words = speak('The forward process adds a little noise at each step.', 'pocket')
assert wav_seconds(wav) > 1 and words, words
unload('tts')
```
